transcript.text: Shark NZ801UK anti hair wrap upright - suction has gone really weak over the last couple of weeks, barely picks up crumbs. Have emptied the bin. Any ideas before I buy a new one?

Switch it off and unplug it (or take the battery off) first. Before you buy a new one, it is probably fixable. Weak suction on Shark vacuums is rarely a motor failure; it is usually airflow being restricted. The next most likely causes are dirty filters or a hidden blockage. 1. Filters: Remove the pre-motor filter and the HEPA filter (usually located near the top of the bin). Wash them in cold water only with no detergent. They must be left to dry completely for at least 24 hours before putting them back. If they are damp, suction will remain weak.
2. Blockages: Detach the hose from the wand and look through it (or shine a torch through it) to ensure nothing is stuck inside. Check the floorhead nozzle and the bin inlet as well. Let me know if you found any blockages or if the filters were clogged/damaged.
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — Lost suction is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage in the hose, tube or floor head — check and clear those before suspecting the motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
Ok. Hose is clear, coin goes straight through and no splits. Never washed the filters though, didn't know they were there. The felt one is caked with fine dust. Will wash them now.

That explains the weak suction – a filter caked in fine dust acts like a brick wall for airflow. Since you’ve just washed them, the critical part is drying. If there is any moisture left inside the foam or felt, it will block air just as effectively as when they were dirty. Please leave them to dry in a warm, airy spot (not on a radiator) for at least 24 hours. Do not put them back until you are sure they are completely dry inside and out. While those are drying, please check the brush bar on the floorhead. Turn it over and look for hair or thread wrapped tightly around the roller. If it is tangled, cut it away with scissors so the brush spins freely by hand. A blocked brush bar also stops pickup. Let me know if the suction returns to normal after that.
Brush bar has a bit of fluff but spins freely, no tangles. Filters are washed, will leave them 24 hours and report back.

It sounds like the caked filter was most likely the main culprit for the gradual loss of suction. We just need to ensure the airflow path is fully restored once those filters are dry. When you put them back in after 24 hours, make sure they are seated firmly – if there's even a small gap around the filter housing, air will leak through that instead of going through the motor, and suction will remain weak. Also, give the bin lid seal a quick wipe to ensure it’s clean so it clicks shut tightly. Once they are dry and reinstalled, try running it on a hard floor (carpet can sometimes mask slight suction issues if the brush bar isn't engaging fully). Let me know if the suction returns to normal or if it's still weak.
Left them 24 hours, put them back and it's a massive difference. Suction is like new. Bin seal looked fine too. No burning smell either.

That is excellent news. It was most likely the caked filters choking the airflow. To keep it running like that for longer, try to wash those filters every month or so before they get completely blocked up again. Is there anything else I can help you with regarding your Shark?
